mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which boosts wage growth and corporate pricing power, driving higher earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and prompts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO contraction months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) signals a disinflationary tightening, which lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such joint events (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS and UNRATE above 4.5% over two months signals strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE > 4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during these episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in HOUST for four consecutive months signals strengthening housing demand, which boosts construction and related industries and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such housing demand expansions (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in GDPC1 for two consecutive quarters signals broad-based demand weakness, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such GDP contraction episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
